title: Quantum Dot (QD)-Modified Carbon Tape Electrodes for Reproducible Electrochemiluminescence (ECL) Emission on a Paper-Based Platform

figure_inventory.scope: Device assembly schematic/photo, not atomic structure
ECL/CV potential context; Ag/AgCl versusSCE conflict

conflicts: Main PDF p.3 Integration specifies an Ag/AgCl reference wire; Figure3 p.4 potential axis is labeled V (vs. SCE). Both statements are retained. The reference scale is unresolved and potentials are not converted.
qualified_source_values: Source reflux80°C retained without pressure inference
1M H2O2 in Figure7 is distinct from1mM in Figure3–5

Source series observation (Main PDF p.4, printed3036, Figure5 discussion): circular coating area increased by approximately60% when QD solution volume increased100%. The exact pair of volumes is not assigned; this is coating geometry, not CdS particle morphology.
Formal Na2S component reference. Materials reports purchased Na2S·9H2O; Methods specifies 4.06 mL of 0.5 M Na2S stock. Stock preparation, aqueous speciation and hydrate geometry are not assigned.
exclusions: Prior cited CdS procedures10/23 are not inspected; this main source supplies its own quantified route.
Electrochemical mechanism equations1–3 are theory/context, not extra material preparation or measured structure.
No graph digitization or inferred absolute ECL intensities; figure labels and prose values retained.
No verified atomic structure, crystal phase or morphology model is supplied for CdS QDs.

qualitative_series_outcomes.source_locator: Main PDF p.4, printed 3036, Results paper-patterning paragraph; Figure2C-D on p.3
qualitative_series_outcomes.observation: Compared with the selected 150 °C / 300 min treatment, the authors report marker diffusion into toner-printed areas at lower temperature or shorter heating duration. This is a qualitative statement about the Figure2 comparison, not a numerical diffusion distance or a universal cutoff assigned to every panel.
qualitative_series_outcomes.scope: Figure2 comparison; no universal cutoff or numerical diffusion assigned.

qualitative_series_outcomes.source_locator: Main PDF p.4, printed 3036, Figure4 electrolyte-volume discussion
qualitative_series_outcomes.observation: ECL increased when running-solution volume rose from 10 to 15 µL and decreased slightly at 20 µL. The authors identify 15 µL as optimal for a thin-layer cell 1.10 cm long and 0.74 cm wide. At lower volume the solution did not cover the entire hydrophilic paper area.
qualitative_series_outcomes.author_interpretation: The authors propose that extra solution leaking outside the thin-layer electrochemical cell explains the change in ECL with increasing electrolyte volume. Leakage is a proposed explanation; its volume is not measured here.

qualitative_series_outcomes.source_locator: Main PDF p.4, printed 3036, H2O2 concentration discussion; Figure6 on p.5
qualitative_series_outcomes.observation: ECL emission was reported as very stable for at least five cycles at all tested H2O2 concentrations in the Figure6 series (0.1, 1, 10 and 100 mM). No additional numerical stability statistic is assigned.

qualitative_series_outcomes.source_locator: Main PDF p.5, printed 3037, dopamine discussion; Figure7A on p.6
qualitative_series_outcomes.observation: Within the Figure7A comparison, ECL intensity decreased as dopamine concentration increased from 1 µM to 10 mM. The zero-dopamine trace is a separate comparison; no absolute intensities are digitized.
qualitative_series_outcomes.author_interpretation: The authors interpret the declining ECL response as dopamine quenching of the CdS-QD ECL system. This source interpretation does not establish a measured molecular binding pose or independently verified mechanism.

figures.caption_paraphrase: 10, 15 and20 µL operating volumes, five scans; this is measurement-solution volume, not CdS coating volume. At lower volume the solution did not cover the entire hydrophilic paper area. The authors propose that extra solution leaking outside the thin-layer electrochemical cell explains the change in ECL with increasing electrolyte volume. Leakage is a proposed explanation; its volume is not measured here.
